**Loss landscapes** — the geometry of trained solutions in weight space — mode connectivity, linear and along curves, barriers between minima and the permutation symmetries that hide or remove them, re-basin alignment, star domains and connecting simplexes, local versus global landscape structure, and model merging as its use (ADR-027).

| [THEORY-105](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-105.md) | Fine-tuning from one pretrained model lands near the edge of a task-specific low-loss region that contains the convex hull of the fine-tuned models, and averaging them moves inward | Gueta et al. (2023), [LIT-658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-658.md): RoBERTa-base models fine-tuned on the same dataset, the same task family, or any of 12 GLUE and SuperGLUE datasets cluster in weight space. Sampled points in the convex hull of each group beat the group's own members in 88% to 96.7% of comparisons. Extrapolating past the members raises the loss quickly, so the members sit near the region's edge and averaging moves inward. The paper calls the region convex, but shows only that the hull lies inside it, by a probe-based loss. Its reading of model soups and SWA as picking points inside the region is argued in its §8, not tested. Moving from the centroid towards the origin stays low-loss far past the members, which the authors cannot explain. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md) | Merging models fine-tuned from one pretrained start loses accuracy through interference in parameter coordinates: redundant small updates dilute the influential ones, and influential updates of different models conflict in sign | Yadav et al. (2023), [LIT-675](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-675.md): keeping only the top 20% of each task vector by magnitude loses almost nothing, so most of an update is redundant. Among the entries that remain, signs conflict between models, more so as more models are merged. Merging (IA)³ models with the multitask model's signs reaches 72.0 against 73.1 for multitask training and 66.4 for TIES with elected signs. That is the strongest evidence that sign is the bottleneck. But the oracle signs come from training on every task's data, the ablation finds rescaling and the disjoint mean matter more than election, and conflicts are as frequent among checkpoints of one task as across tasks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-108](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-108.md) | Across load and temperature, the connectivity and output similarity of independently trained solutions predict test accuracy where endpoint curvature does not: a flat but poorly connected landscape generalizes worse than a connected one of the same curvature | Yang, Hodgkinson, Theisen, Zou, Gonzalez, Ramchandran & Mahoney (2021), [LIT-663](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-663.md): thousands of trained networks on a load by temperature grid, measured by the endpoint Hessian, by mode connectivity on a trained Bezier curve between two independent runs, and by CKA of their outputs. Phases III (flat, poorly connected) and IV-A (flat, connected) have almost the same Hessian and different accuracy; with 10% noisy labels the sharp, unconverged phases beat phase III; label noise barely moves the Hessian while connectivity and CKA fall. One architecture family carries most of it, phases are read by eye, and connectivity alone also fails when the load is data amount. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md) v2 | Along a low-loss linear path between two networks, every layer's features are the interpolation of the endpoints' features, so averaging weights within a basin averages features | Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md): whenever two image classifiers are linearly mode connected, by spawning or by permutation, the features of nearly every layer of the interpolated network are proportional to the interpolation of the endpoints' features. This is layerwise linear feature connectivity, and two conditions, weak additivity of ReLU and a commutativity of weights with features, imply it exactly. Lubana et al.'s Lemma 2, [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md), gives the exact one-hidden-layer case: linear connectivity between interpolating minima forces shared activation patterns, and with shared patterns the hidden features are linear along the path. Measured on pairs at three interpolation points, image classification only. The step to many-model averages such as soups and SWA is not measured. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-113](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-113.md) | Merging models trained on different tasks from different initialisations fails where their features have no counterpart in the other model, and such features grow more common with depth | Stoica et al. (2023), [LIT-665](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-665.md), merge ResNets trained from different initialisations on disjoint label sets. Permute-then-average fails, which they explain by the permuted model lying in a basin for its own task only. Mean cross-model feature correlation falls with depth (0.50, 0.37, 0.27 at three depths). Merging only the early layers and keeping later layers as task heads recovers most of the ensemble's accuracy. Merging features within one model as well as across both helps once the models are wide enough to hold redundant features. | [THEORY-115](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-115.md) v2 | Linear connectivity from a shared, already-stable start holds only when the objectives the runs optimise share structure, and breaks as that structure is removed | Mirzadeh et al. (2020), [LIT-651](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-651.md): from a task-1 solution, a model trained on tasks 1 and 2 together stays on a low task-1 loss line from the start, and one trained on task 2 alone does not. Adding noise to task 2's inputs, corrupting its labels, or removing classes separates the solutions progressively. The authors explain it by curvature: the multitask direction avoids the earlier task's top Hessian eigenvectors. Gueta et al. (2023), [LIT-658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-658.md): fine-tuning runs from one pretrained model are linearly connected within a dataset and a task family. Wen et al. | [THEORY-116](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-116.md) | A linear barrier between two minima that survives the removal of symmetries marks a difference in the input attributes the two models rely on: they compute by different mechanisms | Lubana et al. (2022), [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md): models that rely on a synthetic cue and models that ignore it are separated by a linear barrier even after permutation matching. Fine-tuned models that keep a linear path to their parent keep its cue, and those that lose the path lose the cue. Their Conjecture 1 states this claim's direction. What their Appendix F.3 proves, for a one-hidden-layer ReLU network with interpolating minima, is the converse: linear connectivity forces identical activation patterns, so models relying on attributes of different complexity cannot be linearly connected under any permutation. Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md), support that converse in deep image classifiers, where linearly connected pairs have features that blend layer by layer. The stated direction rests on experiments with synthetic cues and on a one-layer sufficiency argument. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-184](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-184.md) v2 | Under a permutation-equivariant update whose map is K-Lipschitz, coincident neurons stay coincident at every step size, and at step size below 1/K distinct neurons cannot merge in finitely many steps | Yang, Poggio, Chuang and Ziyin (2025), [LIT-861](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-861.md), read in [NOTE-663](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-663.md). If an update commutes with permuting neurons (GD, SGD or Adam on a permutation-symmetric loss) and its map is K-Lipschitz, one step of size η changes every pairwise neuron distance by a factor in [1 − ηK, 1 + ηK]. This is a proved constraint on trajectories. It does not say that training simplifies above 1/K, that neurons never merge in the limit, or that any scale-dependent shape of the neuron cloud is preserved. | Active |
| [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md) | A converged network trained with SGD is not at a point and does not sample its training loss: under a quadratic approximation it samples a Gibbs distribution on a modified loss, isotropic in the Hessian's column space, with probability currents that keep it oscillating, so its speed and spread are set by the learning rate, momentum and batch size | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md). Modelled as an underdamped Langevin equation with noise covariance proportional to the Hessian, SGD at the end of training converges to a nonequilibrium stationary state: Gibbs on a modified loss whose curvature undoes the Hessian's anisotropy, with inverse temperature S(1 − β²), in broken detailed balance. A ResNet-18 on ImageNet explores isotropically in a plane where the loss is anisotropic, oscillates at Hessian-dependent rates, and moves at the predicted speed across a hyperparameter sweep. For the learned-structure line, a trained solution is in part a property of the regime that trained it. Proposed: the deep-learning evidence is one network, under assumptions the paper concedes are strained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-210](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-210.md) v2 | Continuous parameter symmetries stretch a network's minima into connected manifolds along which the loss is flat, and give gradient flow conserved quantities that fix where on such a manifold training ends; finite steps, gradient noise and weight decay break them, so the position along a symmetry orbit is set by initialization and optimizer, not by the loss | Zhao, Walters & Yu (2025), [LIT-970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-970.md), read in [NOTE-712](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-712.md): a survey, so the dynamical results are secondhand. Continuous parameter-space symmetries (GL, scaling, orthogonal, translation) make minima positive-dimensional and connected, which is one source of mode connectivity. Under gradient flow each gives a conserved quantity, such as layer imbalance, that is fixed by initialization and locates the endpoint on the manifold. Under SGD these are not conserved. Read first-hand (Neural Mechanics; Ziyin et al.), weight decay drives the conserved quantities toward zero, and minibatch noise drives a rescaling symmetry's toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances. The survey had reported this as imbalance decaying with large learning rates, and a stationary distribution biased toward balanced solutions that a Langevin model does not predict. This is the null-space half that [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md)'s limiting dynamics leave out. Proposed: one survey, with the SGD results unread here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md) v2 | In the stochastic-differential-equation model of SGD, with a gradient-noise covariance that depends on the parameters, minibatch noise drives the difference of squared norms along a rescaling symmetry, at a rate proportional to learning rate over batch size, to the point on the symmetry orbit where the gradient-noise traces of the two parameter groups are equal, whenever both groups carry noise; so at stationarity SGD neither keeps the difference fixed, as gradient flow does, nor lets it diffuse, as isotropic noise does, and differs from gradient descent by a finite amount however small the noise | Ziyin, Li & Ueda ([LIT-1012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1012.md), read in [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md)), with the gradient flow conservation law and the Itô term from Neural Mechanics ([LIT-1013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1013.md)). If ℓ(u, w) = ℓ(λu, w/λ) for every sample, then under the SDE model of SGD d(‖u‖² − ‖w‖²)/dt = −T(uᵀC₁u − wᵀC₂w), with T = η/S. The noise has no component along the symmetry, but its dependence on the parameters produces a deterministic drift through Itô's lemma. The drift points to the noise-balanced point, and weight decay adds to its rate. In a diagonal linear network the stationary distribution follows exactly: it is non-ergodic, has a memory of initialization, and collapses to zero above a critical temperature. The law is re-derived here (2026-10-19) within the SDE model; the tests are small synthetic networks, and whether it holds in deep networks on real data is QUESTION-164. | Active |
| [THEORY-213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-213.md) v2 | Every mirror symmetry of a network's per-sample loss makes its symmetric subspace invariant under gradient descent and SGD, and when the loss's Hessian is bounded below by −c, weight decay γ‖θ‖² with γ > c/2 puts every minimum in that subspace; rescaling symmetries that hold at λ = −1, rotation symmetries and permutation symmetries contain such mirrors, whose subspaces are zeroed weights, reduced rank and identical neurons | Ziyin (2024), [LIT-1014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1014.md), read in [NOTE-716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-716.md). If a per-sample loss is invariant under the reflection I − 2OOᵀ, then Oᵀθ = 0 is a stationary condition for GD and SGD. The Hessian is block diagonal there. Above a critical weight decay all minima satisfy the constraint. Under SGD with strong noise the subspace is attractive even at a strict saddle, by a Lyapunov-exponent argument. Rescaling, rotation and permutation symmetries imply mirrors, so they yield sparsity, low rank and merged neurons, with collapse and loss of plasticity as consequences. The SGD half is approximate and the network evidence is limited; the title holds only the exact half. Promoted on 2026-10-20 on the exact half, re-derived. The SGD half is QUESTION-206. | Active |
| [THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md) v2 | Under MSE loss, in Han, Papyan and Donoho's VGG, ResNet and DenseNet runs on five balanced ten-class datasets, the trained classifier stays near the least-squares classifier for its own features from an early epoch; and on that central path, for unconstrained features continually renormalized to identity within-class covariance and without weight decay, gradient flow drives the class-separation singular values to infinity at equal rates, which in that model is neural collapse | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). MSE loss splits exactly into a least-squares term and a non-negative deviation term, and the deviation becomes negligible early in training in 15 dataset–network cells. On that central path, with λ = 0, the loss is ½ Σ 1/(ω_j² + C) in the singular values of Σ_W^(−1/2)M̃. Under a flow that re-whitens the features after every step, each ω_j grows as (4t/N)^(1/4), and their ratios tend to 1. That is NC1 and NC2, and NC3–NC4 follow. Not shown: that ordinary training is this flow, or anything for cross-entropy or with weight decay. | Active |
| [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md) v2 | Under class imbalance the last-layer geometry that unregularized cross-entropy prefers is not the simplex ETF but simplex-encoded-label interpolation: the logits equal the simplex-encoded labels, the classifier and embedding Gram matrices come from that matrix's SVD, any finite weight decay changes the geometry, and training approaches it more slowly as imbalance grows | Thrampoulidis et al. | [THEORY-425](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-425.md) | A connecting path trained only on clean data keeps only the behaviour the clean data ask for: between two backdoored or error-injected image classifiers, models near the ends of such a path keep most clean accuracy and lose the attack, and a path flat in ordinary loss can carry a barrier in adversarial loss that tracks the input Hessian's top eigenvalue | Zhao, Chen, Das, Ramamurthy & Lin (2020), [LIT-668](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-668.md), read in [NOTE-530](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-530.md). | [THEORY-509](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-509.md) | Under genericity conditions, two dense or top-k (k ≥ 2) mixture-of-experts layers compute the same function only if they differ by a permutation of the experts with their gates and a common translation of the gate weights, and the translation leaves every interpolation barrier unchanged, so expert order is the only gate symmetry alignment must undo | Tran, Trinh, Bui & Nguyen (2025), [LIT-670](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-670.md), read in [NOTE-513](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-513.md). | [THEORY-521](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-521.md) | In the thermodynamic limit, with examples and capacity growing together at fixed load, generalization error can jump discontinuously with the load when the entropy of hypotheses just above the best error vanishes faster than the training-error energy grows: a spherical perceptron's error falls smoothly as 1/α, an Ising perceptron's drops to zero at a critical load | Martin & Mahoney (2017), [LIT-672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-672.md), read in [NOTE-542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-542.md), restating Seung, Sompolinsky & Tishby (1992) and Haussler, Kearns, Seung & Tishby (1996), which the record does not hold. (2022), [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md), Lemma 2: for one hidden layer and interpolating minima, linear mode connectivity forces shared activation patterns, and with shared patterns the hidden features are linear along the path. It says nothing about when the conditions hold. That trained pairs satisfy them is [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md)'s empirical claim. | Active |
| [THEORY-736](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-736.md) | Two ε-dropout-stable solutions of a multilayer ReLU net, under a loss convex in the output, are joined by a piecewise-linear path whose loss never exceeds the worse endpoint's by more than ε, and joined pairwise paths compose with no higher barrier than their worst | Kuditipudi et al. (2019), [LIT-671](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-671.md), Theorem 1, read in full in [NOTE-544](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-544.md), with Draxler et al.'s (2018) concatenation bound from [LIT-653](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-653.md). Dropout stability gives every solution a half-width copy with the same loss up to ε. Half the units are then free, so working units can be swapped in and permuted at no cost. That joins any two such solutions. It is a statement about dropout-stable solutions only: whether training produces them is [THEORY-109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-109.md)'s open question, and Theorem 4 of the same paper builds disconnected global minima. | Active |
| [THEORY-741](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-741.md) | A two-layer ReLU student of width at least kM, fitting an orthonormal teacher of M neurons on the sphere, has for any k global minima a global minimum joined to each by a two-piece linear path of minima; and in a deep linear network of depth L and width above 1 + r(L − 1), any r global minima in general position share a global minimum linearly connected to each | Lin, Li and Wu (2024), [LIT-682](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-682.md), Theorems 6, 11 and 18 with Lemmas 7 and 25, read in [NOTE-535](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-535.md) and re-derived by the promotion audit. Two toy models whose minima can be written down: a two-layer ReLU student of an orthonormal teacher on the sphere at population loss, and a deep linear network fitting y = Qx. Spare width lets every minimum be moved, along segments of minima, to one a common centre can reach. No permutation symmetry is used, and nothing is claimed about trained networks. | Active |
